GRADUATE APPLICATION PROCEDURES
In order to apply to our graduate program, you must apply to the University of South
Florida Graduate Program and choose one of the degree programs/majors: PhD in Computer
Science and Engineering, PhD in Data Science and AI, MS in Computer Science, MS in
Computer Engineering, or MS in Cyber Security. Just follow the instructions included
in this link.
A PDF of GRE Scores is required for all MS majors (excluding MSAI), unless the applicant
has an undergraduate degree from ABET-accredited degree programs, or from a Carnegie
R1 university, or for applicants who have successfully completed USF Pathway to Computing
(PTC) Graduate Certificate.
For more information on the requirements of each program, please read the catalogs
linked below:
PhD in Computer Science and Engineering (PhD CSE)
PhD in Data Science and AI (formerly PhD in Big Data Analytics)
Master of Science in Computer Science (MSCS)
Master of Science in Computer Engineering (MSCP)
Master of Science in Computer Science and Engineering (MSCSE)
Master of Science in Cybersecurity (MSCYS)
Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence (MSAI)
A complete application includes:
Unofficial Transcripts (including the grade sheet and diploma, if applicable)
PDF of GRE Scores (for Master's applicants except MSAI)
Resume
Statement of Purpose
3 Letters of Recommendation (Must be on official letterhead with recommender’s title
and contact)
PDF of English Proficiency Scores, if applicable
If admitted, official transcripts and test scores will need to be submitted to Graduate
Admissions but unofficial transcripts/scores can be used in reviewing the application.
Note to PhD students seeking Post-Master’s status: If you would like to be considered
for Post-Master’s status and you have an international Master’s degree, you need to
formally evaluate your degree using evaluation services such as WES or NACES or any
other services of your choice. The payment for such evaluations is the student’s or
supervisor’s responsibility.
Out of College Co-Major Supervisors and RAship
Out-of-college faculty (with or without an affiliate position in Bellini College)
initiate participation by forming a research collaboration with a Bellini College
faculty member in a closely aligned area. The Bellini faculty member will serve as
the Major Supervisor, admit the PhD student, and assume primary advising responsibility;
the out-of-college faculty member may serve as co-advisor on the collaborative project.
While external resources may fully or partially support the work, all RA payments
must be processed through a subcontract to Bellini College directed to the Major Supervisor.
This structure ensures the student is embedded in Bellini’s PhD program while advancing
a jointly led research agenda (shared mentoring, publications, and lab integration).
Graduate Application Deadline
Please see the Office of Graduate Studies website for priority deadlines.
We offer fall and spring admissions for all of our MSc and PhD degrees.
MS and PhD priority deadlines:
Fall: January 15
Spring: September 1
Please see the Office of Admission website for the final university deadlines.
MS final university deadlines:
Fall: June 1
Spring: October 15
PhD final university deadlines:
Fall: February 15
Spring: October 15
Applications received by the priority deadline will receive maximum consideration.
Applications received after the priority deadline, but by the final university deadline,
are considered on a space-available basis. All supporting materials must be received
by the stated deadlines.
If you intend to apply for the USF OGS fellowships administered at university-level,
you may need to apply earlier than the priority deadline so that you have sufficient
time after your admission to apply. The list of OGS fellowships is here: https://www.usf.edu/graduate-studies/funding/fellowships-scholarships/index.aspx
For questions regarding applying to our graduate programs, please visit the Advising page to contact a Graduate Advisor.
